description: 🚀 ExtraTerrestrial Martians is a team of passionate students interested in space exploration, technology, and creative problem-solving. We're building an engaging project for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, combining web development, research, and interactive storytelling.
summary:
AFTERLIFE: The Forgotten Space Museum is an interactive digital museum dedicated to preserving and exploring the stories of human-made space hardware that has completed its mission, lost communication, run out of power, or remained on celestial bodies.

Inspired by NASA's challenge “Abandoned but not Forgotten,” AFTERLIFE brings together the stories of historic spacecraft, lunar landers, rovers, scientific instruments, and other space technologies across the Solar System.

Through an immersive, visually interactive experience, visitors can explore these artifacts, understand their missions, discover where they are today, and learn about the scientific and historical legacy they left behind.

Our project aims to transform scattered mission information into an engaging journey through humanity's technological footprint in space, reminding people that even when a mission ends, its contribution to science and exploration continues.
details:
What is AFTERLIFE?

AFTERLIFE is an interactive digital museum that documents humanity's legacy of space exploration through spacecraft, landers, rovers, scientific instruments, and other human-made objects that remain beyond Earth.

How does it work?

The platform organizes space artifacts and missions into an immersive exploration experience. Users can discover objects left on the Moon and Mars, explore the stories behind historic missions, and understand what happened to the hardware after its original mission ended.

Instead of presenting these objects as isolated facts, AFTERLIFE connects them to the larger story of human exploration, scientific discovery, and technological progress.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Preserves the historical and scientific stories of inactive and retired space hardware.
  • Makes space exploration history more accessible and engaging.
  • Helps users understand the difference between completed missions, inactive hardware, lost communication, and objects intentionally left behind.
  • Encourages curiosity about planetary exploration and humanity's long-term footprint beyond Earth.
  • Provides an engaging educational experience for students, educators, and space enthusiasts.

NASA Resources and Research

Our research draws on NASA's mission documentation, spacecraft records, historical information, and official image archives. These resources helped us identify and document the stories of lunar modules, lunar rovers, ALSEP experiments, Surveyor, Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity, Viking, InSight, Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer, Kepler, and Ingenuity.

Technology and Development

The project was developed as a web-based interactive experience using our team's web development tools and AI-assisted development workflow.

The website is hosted on Github Pages, with the source code maintained in GitHub.

Creativity and Design Approach

AFTERLIFE approaches space history as a digital museum rather than a conventional information portal. Its visual storytelling, interactive navigation, and immersive presentation aim to make forgotten space hardware feel like meaningful pieces of humanity's shared history.

The central idea is simple: missions may end, but their legacy does not.
